data.title: Convano's (TSE:6574) Conservative Accounting Might Explain Soft Earnings
data.description:
Investors were disappointed with the weak earnings posted by Convano Inc. (TSE:6574 ). Despite the soft profit numbers, our analysis has optimistic about the overall quality of the income statement.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

A Closer Look At Convano's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Convano recorded an accrual ratio of -1.82. That implies it has very good cash conversion, and that its earnings in the last year actually significantly understate its free cash flow. In fact, it had free cash flow of JP¥12b in the last year, which was a lot more than its statutory profit of JP¥216.0m. Given that Convano had negative free cash flow in the prior corresponding period, the trailing twelve month resul of JP¥12b would seem to be a step in the right direction. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

In a scenario where those unusual items included non-cash charges, we'd expect to see a strong accrual ratio, which is exactly what has happened in this case. It's never great to see unusual items costing the company profits, but on the upside, things might improve sooner rather than later. When we analysed the vast majority of listed companies worldwide, we found that significant unusual items are often not repeated. All else being equal, this would likely have the effect of making the statutory profit look worse than its underlying earnings power.

Our Take On Convano's Profit Performance

data.title: Horizon Gold Eyes 2028 Production As Development Plans Advance
data.description:
Key points:

  • Horizon Gold has completed a Definitive Feasibility Study for its 100%-owned Gum Creek Gold Project, outlining a 10-year open-pit operation targeting 880,000 ounces of recovered gold.
  • Based on a gold price of $5,500 per ounce, Gum Creek is forecast to generate $1.85 billion in pre-tax free cash flow, with a projected pre-tax NPV of A$1.31 billion.
  • Horizon is targeting a Final Investment Decision in the June quarter of 2027, with construction potentially starting later that year and first gold targeted for the second half of 2028.
  • The project requires approximately A$350 million in pre-production capital expenditure, with Horizon appointing specialist adviser Orimco to manage a competitive financing process.

On Friday, Western Australian gold exploration stock, Horizon Gold (ASX:HRN), held its annual general meeting, providing an update on its progress towards becoming a gold producer.

The company has completed a Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS) for its 100%-owned Gum Creek Gold Project, outlining plans for a 10-year open-pit operation capable of producing an estimated 880,000 ounces of gold.

Horizon is now working towards a Final Investment Decision (FID) in the June quarter of 2027, with construction potentially starting later that year and first gold targeted for the second half of 2028.

Gum Creek outlines a sizeable gold mining opportunity

Horizon Gold released its feasibility study in July, which estimated a potential 880,000 ounces of gold recovered over a ten-year mine life, averaging around 98,000 ounces per year over the first five years.

Based on a gold price of $5,500 per ounce, the project is forecast to generate $1.85 billion in pre-tax free cash flow over its initial 10-year mine life. It also carries a projected pre-tax net present value (NPV) of $1.31 billion and an internal rate of return (IRR) of 53.1%, with an estimated payback period of 23 months from first production.

The project assumes an all-in sustaining cost of around $2,995 per ounce, suggesting that, assuming gold prices as projected, the operation could retain substantial profit margins.

It should be noted that these figures are projected figures based on assumptions, and that reality could differ significantly, which would change the economic viability of the mine.

The next steps of Horizon Gold’s Gum Creek project

Of course, being a successful mining stock requires more than a feasibility study.

Now that its definitive feasibility study is complete, the company is turning its attention to the practical steps required to bring Gum Creek into production.

The company is targeting a Final Investment Decision in the June quarter of 2027, with construction expected to begin in late 2027, subject to funding and approvals. While the approval processes have commenced, engineering work is also progressing.

However, financing will be a critical focus.

Horizon Gold estimates that the project will require around $350 million in capital expenditure before the mine produces anything. The company raised $30 million in March to fund exploration and other pre-development activities, and has around $16.9 million in cash at the end of December, so further financing is likely.

Horizon has appointed specialist adviser Orimco to manage a competitive financing process, with discussions underway to secure a suitable funding package. The eventual solution could involve debt, equity, or a combination of funding sources, although further equity issuance could dilute existing shareholders.

Is Horizon Gold approaching a key catalyst?

These next 12 to 18 months are likely to be an important period for Horizon as it looks to move from a gold exploration company towards becoming a gold-producing company.

Gum Creek provides a defined starting point, with a 10-year mine plan and scope for further growth through additional deposits and ongoing exploration. If the company can secure development funding and deliver the project as planned, it could establish a new revenue stream from late 2028.

This can be seen by analysts forecasting revenue to start being generated in late 2028 or early 2029 calendar years, with potential earnings coming later in 2029. However, these projections remain dependent on Horizon securing the necessary capital, completing construction, and achieving its production targets.

For investors considering this small-cap ASX gold stock, the opportunity lies in what Horizon could become, while the risks remain firmly tied to what it still needs to deliver and how it can fund the items it needs to do to get there.

For Horizon, gold discovery is important, but getting Gum Creek into production could matter even more.

data.title: TechMatrix's (TSE:3762) Promising Earnings May Rest On Soft Foundations
data.description:
TechMatrix Corporation's (TSE:3762) robust earnings report didn't manage to move the market for its stock. Our analysis suggests that this might be because shareholders have noticed some concerning underlying factors.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against TechMatrix's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

For the year to September 2026, TechMatrix had an accrual ratio of 0.45. That means it didn't generate anywhere near enough free cash flow to match its profit. Statistically speaking, that's a real negative for future earnings. In fact, it had free cash flow of JP¥3.2b in the last year, which was a lot less than its statutory profit of JP¥5.45b. TechMatrix shareholders will no doubt be hoping that its free cash flow bounces back next year, since it was down over the last twelve months. The good news for shareholders is that TechMatrix's accrual ratio was much better last year, so this year's poor reading might simply be a case of a short term mismatch between profit and FCF. As a result, some shareholders may be looking for stronger cash conversion in the current year.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On TechMatrix's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, we think TechMatrix's earnings were not supported by free cash flow, which might concern some investors. As a result, we think it may well be the case that TechMatrix's underlying earnings power is lower than its statutory profit. Nonetheless, it's still worth noting that its earnings per share have grown at 64% over the last three years.
